wu: Flashcard Race: Students line up in two teams. Teacher shows a flashcard of a morning routine action (e.g., 'brush teeth'), first student to shout the English word and mime it gets a point for their team.
wuAlt: Morning Charades: One student mimes a morning action (e.g., 'wake up'), others guess the English word.
Quick Review Bingo: Each student draws a 3x3 grid with words like 'wash', 'eat', 'go to school'. Teacher calls out actions, students cross them off first to shout 'Bingo!'
pres: Teacher uses a big storybook with pictures of a child's morning routine. 'Look! Sam wakes up at 7 o'clock. He washes his face. He brushes his teeth.' Teacher points to a clock and says '7 o'clock'. Students repeat chorally. Teacher asks 'What time does Sam wake up?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Realia Demo: Teacher brings a toothbrush, soap, and a toy clock. 'I wake up at 6 o'clock. I wash my face. I brush my teeth.' Students repeat actions and sentences.
Video Clip: Show a short, silent video of a morning routine. Teacher narrates: 'He wakes up. He eats breakfast. He goes to school.'
prac: Clock Matching Game: In pairs, students have a set of clock faces (o'clock/half past) and sentence cards ('I eat at 8 o'clock'). They match the clocks to the sentences. Teacher circulates to help with pronunciation and time vocabulary.
pracAlt: Sentence Dominoes: Students have dominoes with a time on one half and a morning action on the other (e.g., '7:00' | 'wake up'). They take turns connecting them to make a logical sequence.
Routine Relay: Two lines of students. Teacher whispers a sentence like 'I brush my teeth' to the first student. They whisper it down the line. Last student runs to the board and writes/draws it.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher reads a short story: 'I wake up at 7 o'clock. I eat breakfast at 7:30. I go to school at 8 o'clock.' Students draw the three events in order on a piece of paper with three empty clock faces. Teacher checks drawings for correct sequence.
re: Action Race: After the break, students stand. Teacher calls out a time (e.g., '8 o'clock!') and an action (e.g., 'go to school!'). Students must mime the action and say the sentence 'I go to school at 8 o'clock!' The fastest group gets a point.
prod: My Morning Timeline Project: In groups of three, students draw and write a 4-step timeline of their own morning routine using sentence starters like 'I wake up at ___. I eat at ___.' Each group presents their timeline to the class, pointing and reading their sentences.
rw: Read and Match: Students read a short paragraph: 'My name is Fatima. I wake up at 6:30. I eat cereal. I go to school at 7:45.' They then match the paragraph to the correct set of three clock faces (6:30, 7:00, 7:45) by drawing a line.
st: Teacher tells a simple story using a felt board: 'The Lazy Lion's Morning'. The lion wakes up late, rushes, and forgets to brush his teeth. The story uses target vocabulary. End with the 'Goodbye Song' (e.g., 'See You Later Alligator'), updating the sticker chart, and a high-five line as students exit.
g: Students have bingo cards with clock faces. Teacher calls out times ('half past seven'), students cover the matching clock.

One student is 'Mr. Wolf', back to the class. Class chants 'What's the time, Mr. Wolf?' He answers a time (e.g., '8 o'clock') and class takes that many steps. If he says 'dinnertime!', he chases them.
Two teams race to put a set of picture cards in the correct morning order (wake up, wash, eat, go to school).
Students play in pairs. A grid has times in the boxes. Student A says a sentence ('I eat at 8 o'clock') to claim a box with '8 o'clock'.
Students turn over cards with morning actions and times. They must match a picture of 'brushing teeth' with a card saying '7:30'.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 5-sentence paragraph about their sibling's morning routine using 'He/She' and times.
Support / weaker learners: Use a word bank with pictures to fill in the blanks in sentences like 'I ___ at 7 o'clock.' (wake up/wash/eat).
hw: Interview a family member about their morning routine and write down 2 answers in English (e.g., 'My dad wakes up at 5:30 AM.', 'My mom drinks tea for breakfast').
Draw a picture of your family eating breakfast and write one sentence about it (e.g., 'We eat at 7:30 AM').
Make a paper clock and show the time you usually go to school.
tip: Use the local context of Ramadan to discuss morning routines before dawn (Suhoor), connecting the lesson to students' lives and making the language more meaningful.
